## Highlights

This release makes `refresh_state()` report what it reads, lets callers refresh only the attributes they need, keeps `ws_listen()` running when a single update fails, and reports unreadable datapoint values as unknown (`None`) instead of raising or falling back to `0`.

### `refresh_state()` notifies callbacks (#332)

`refresh_state()` now caches the values it reads and notifies the callbacks of every refreshed attribute once per call, even when the values did not change. Attributes that report commands (button presses, `requested_*` values, a cover's `target_position`) are refreshed without notification. In Home Assistant, `update_entity` therefore updates all entities of the channel, not only the one named in the action.

### Refresh only the requested attributes (#335)

`refresh_state()` accepts an optional `attributes` argument with callback-attribute names, the same names used by `register_callback()`. Channels that map their attributes to datapoints read only the datapoints behind those attributes. For example, `refresh_state(attributes=["force"])` on a wind sensor makes one request instead of three. Only the requested attributes are refreshed and notified, so other attributes of the channel keep their current values.

- The wind sensor and air quality sensor support this so far. Other channels, and any attribute without a mapping, still refresh every datapoint.
- Calling `refresh_state()` without `attributes`, or with an empty list, refreshes everything as before.
- A single string, such as `refresh_state(attributes="force")`, is treated as one attribute name.
- An unknown attribute name raises `UnknownCallbackAttributeException` before any request is sent.

### `UnknownCallbackAttributeException` message

The message no longer assumes the attribute was being registered, and the "atrribute" typo is fixed. It now reads, for example, `Unknown callback-attribute 'not_there'; known callback-attributes: 'state,alarm,force'.`

### Errors in WebSocket updates are isolated (#331)

Previously, an exception while handling one datapoint or one subscriber callback aborted `FreeAtHome.update()`, so the rest of the message was dropped, and the exception ended `ws_listen()`. Such errors are now logged with their traceback and skipped. The rest of the message is still applied and the listener keeps running.

- Each datapoint, channel attribute callback, device availability callback, parameter callback, and devices-changed callback is isolated, so one failing subscriber no longer blocks the others.
- Malformed WebSocket frames and exceptions from the message callback are logged instead of ending `ws_listen()`. Connection errors are handled as before.
- `asyncio.CancelledError` is not caught, so cancelling the listener still works.

### Unparseable values no longer raise in more channels (#329)

Several channels parsed numeric datapoints with a bare `float()` or `int()`, so a value such as `"invalid"` or `""` raised `ValueError`. This failed `FreeAtHome.load()` or ended `ws_listen()`. These values are now `None`, as they already were for `TemperatureSensor` and the valve actuators. This applies to:

- `RoomTemperatureController` `state_indication` and `eco_mode`, and `VirtualRoomTemperatureController` `eco_mode`, `target_temperature`, and `current_temperature`
- `DimmingActuator.brightness` and `ColorTemperatureActuator.color_temperature`
- `WindSensor`, `BrightnessSensor`, `AirQualitySensor`, and `MovementDetector` readings
- `CoverActuator.position` and `ShutterActuator.tilt_position`

An overflowing value such as `"inf"` is also unknown for brightness, color temperature, and cover positions.

### Unreadable virtual sensor values are unknown (#340, #324)

The virtual brightness, temperature, wind, energy battery, energy inverter, and two-way meter channels now report `None` instead of `0` when a datapoint value is not a number, such as an empty value. `0` could not be told apart from a real reading such as 0 °C or an energy counter of 0 kWh. This matches the physical sensors, which already report `None`.

- Code that compares or calculates with these values must handle `None`.
- A `None` value, and an overflowing brightness such as `"inf"`, are now unknown too instead of raising an exception.

### Unreadable heating and cooling values are unknown (#341, #324)

`RoomTemperatureController.heating` and `cooling`, including `RadiatorActuator.heating` from its heating demand, now report `None` instead of `0` when the value is not a number, such as an empty value. A reported `0` still means idle.

- Code that compares or calculates with these values must handle `None`. `RadiatorActuator.heating_active` treats an unknown heating demand as not active, as it did with `0`.
- A `None` value, and an overflowing value such as `"inf"`, are now unknown too instead of raising an exception.
